coaching.headline: We won every lane, then gave away a full wipe and two free majors before conversion pulled it home.
coaching.team: Every lane read favored, and the early game backed it up: Early Fangtooth wins built a lead, even though the 2v1 loss to Rampage at 2.7 minutes was the wrong fight to take that early. The lead cracked between 24.3 and 25.7, when all five players died in succession and the enemy took the resulting Primal Fangtooth. Two more majors were handed over for nothing: Genesis Core at 28 and another Primal Fangtooth at 43 both fell with nobody of ours dead — five living players just weren't there. Even so, the team out-converted the opponent, converting five of six won fights against their five of eight, and closed 13 towers to 7. A clean 0-4 loss at Orb Prime in the 41.6-minute fight came while sitting far ahead on items, proof that stretch was a decision problem, not a gear one. Next game: hold vision and get bodies to a major before it spawns, instead of arriving only after the fight meant to stop it.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: Five deaths between 24.3 and 25.7 handed the enemy their Primal Fangtooth and erased the early lead; the fights the team did win still converted at five of six, which is what pulled the game back.
coaching.whatWorked: Conversion: five of six won fights cashed inside 90 seconds against the opponent's five of eight — that gap is why 13 towers fell to their 7.

perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Murdock was the closer: 14 kills against 4 deaths, with solo picks at 27.5 and 46.3, plus a shared kill with Scarlett at 30.7, that won fights outright. His build matched the community's winning core (Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher, Imperator) exactly before adding late rounds items on top.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Scarlett anchored the jungle's objective game, 56,949 damage to objectives, more than her own hero damage, but built zero magic resist into a comp running three magical damage sources — the same gap as a recent film's zero armor against three physical damage dealers. Died five times, twice to Akeron — the 26-minute Primal Fangtooth loss came in a fight the team opened already two players down, not from her death alone.
perPlayer.efa63e55-9c51-43fe-8048-30ac11856e0a: Zarus lost the individual matchup badly: two kills in 47 minutes, and five of his eight deaths were to the same hero, Akeron, in a lane the draft read as favored the whole game. One, at 12.2, was a solo catch away from the team; separately, the 25.7 death came in a fight the team opened already two players down, and the 41.7 death fed the enemy's Primal Fangtooth at 43 minutes.
perPlayer.8fae7ec7-62b2-40b6-a1e1-181d0d016a82: Valmont led the entire match in damage to heroes at 77,549, ahead of Gideon's 76,126, and personally accounted for six of Riktor's eight deaths. The cost was nine deaths of his own, including a solo catch at 11.3, feeding four separate objective losses.
perPlayer.aa418bf7-44c2-44f9-ad6a-58ee702a6474: Kwang held the frontline but lost the vision fight: 68,013 mitigated and 47% kill participation against 17 wards placed to Riktor's 27, in a vision war the team lost 56 to 69 with just one of the enemy's wards destroyed. Two of his own deaths came before minute 10, and he died first in two fights.

33.3.call: The best fight of the game: the 33.3-minute teamfight at their Inner Tower, won 4-1 — that's what a won fight should look like.

39.6.call: Taking the tower while Orb Prime fell elsewhere was the right trade — three kills and a structure beats one uncontested buff.

41.6.call: Losing this 0-4 with the item lead, 24 to 12, was the costliest read of the game — nothing to win there, the fight should have been skipped.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Murdock's full core matched the community's winning path exactly: Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher, Imperator (56.5% winrate at that build), then Tainted Rounds and Nuclear Rounds added pure damage on top. Nothing missing from the core; the late kills at 27.5, 30.7, and 46.3 back up that the build was working.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Murdock's low-mobility poke kit leans on a burst-window Eternal loadout that rewards staying at range behind Zarus and Kwang's frontline, trading dueling sustain for the pick power he actually used late.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Scarlett's full build, Manta Scythe, Malady, Earthshaker, Nightfall, Infernum, and Syonic Echo, carried no magic resist at all, flagged directly against a comp running three magical damage sources. That gap lines up with two late deaths to Akeron, in fights where the team was already down bodies before she died.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: There's no established meta core for this Scarlett build to compare against, so the engine's jungle Eternal read leans on general objective-clear and dueling fit rather than a proven in-game swap.

efa63e55-9c51-43fe-8048-30ac11856e0a.build: Zarus skipped two of his winning core's three items, Augmentation and Mutilator, the ability-haste and lifesteal pieces his sustained-duel kit wants, building early tank items instead. Against an Akeron who beat him five times, that gap in sustain shows up in the deaths.
efa63e55-9c51-43fe-8048-30ac11856e0a.eternal: Zarus's engine Eternal loadout leans into the Coliseum-trap duel his kit is built around, favoring sustained one-on-one power over teamfight utility — a trade against a root-heavy Akeron matchup that punished him five times.

8fae7ec7-62b2-40b6-a1e1-181d0d016a82.build: There's no tracked meta core for this hero to compare against, so build is un-gradeable here — on results alone it produced the match's highest hero damage and six kills on Riktor.
8fae7ec7-62b2-40b6-a1e1-181d0d016a82.eternal: Valmont's Eternal read is theory only here too — the kit data doesn't carry his combo or synergy detail, so the fit call is general midlane burst-vs-sustain rather than anything tied to this game's fights.

aa418bf7-44c2-44f9-ad6a-58ee702a6474.build: Kwang skipped the full meta core, Spirit of Amir, Oathkeeper, and Tainted Scepter, the healing-and-utility path, for a tankier Combustion-into-Warden's-Faith build instead. That trade shows in the numbers: modest healing at 9,094 but heavy mitigation at 68,013, a frontline read over a peel read.
aa418bf7-44c2-44f9-ad6a-58ee702a6474.eternal: Support Eternals like Exarch, Aion, Lotus, Marrow, Nihil, Weald, Pilow, and Satariel aren't modeled by the engine, so there's no fit read for Kwang here — only the field position, frontline bruiser-support, is known.

threats: Chain-CC risk (4 hard-CC abilities, ~3.5s of lockdown): Akeron Web Lash (root 1s), Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Kwang Surge of the Heavens (knockup 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Kwang) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Static Trap root → Buckshot → Hot Pursuit AS → Long Arm of the Law global snipe
ourKits.winCondition: trap for the root, then out-range with Shots Fired and finish with the global ult
ourKits.passive: every 5th basic is a long-range bonus shot
ourKits.playWith: frontline/peel to protect his low mobility
ourKits.playAgainst: almost no escape — engage past the trap and he dies

ourKits.combo: Evade in → Barricade block → Spear of Nyr (execute <20%) → Coliseum ult arena
ourKits.winCondition: trap a target in Coliseum and out-duel with stacked Gladiator
ourKits.playWith: a team that joins him inside the Coliseum
ourKits.playAgainst: don't fight him in his arena — disengage; burst through Barricade's window

ourKits.combo: Judgement tether → Surge knockup → Fury of the Heavens slow, recall the blade
ourKits.winCondition: tether a target, knock up and brawl with energized basics
ourKits.playWith: follow-up while he tethers and knocks up
ourKits.playAgainst: bait his blade-recall mobility, then punish when it's placed

enemyKits.combo: Web Lash root → Crushing Maw armor shred → Hellfire eye → Consume pull-channel
enemyKits.winCondition: root with Web Lash and grind with Hunger-stacked haste
enemyKits.playWith: follow-up burst on his rooted target
enemyKits.playAgainst: dodge Web Lash — without the root he has no lock-down; interrupt Consume

enemyKits.combo: stance-swap with Zero Shift → Tachyon Lance (ranged) or melee chain → Limit Break on Overheat
enemyKits.winCondition: build Heat and burst with Limit Break, flexing range and melee
enemyKits.passive: damage builds Heat → Overheat unlocks Limit Break
enemyKits.playWith: peel that lets her ramp Heat safely
enemyKits.playAgainst: pressure her before Overheat; CC during the melee stance

enemyKits.combo: Void Breach slow → Cosmic Rift → Black Hole on the grouped enemies
enemyKits.winCondition: land Black Hole / Cosmic Rift on a clumped team for AoE burst
enemyKits.passive: an ability-empowered basic tethers a target for bonus damage
enemyKits.playWith: hard engage that clumps enemies into his Black Hole
enemyKits.playAgainst: immobile with long cooldowns — dodge the skillshots and dive him once Black Hole is down

enemyKits.combo: Riplash pull → Shock Therapy silence → Skewer suppress ult
enemyKits.winCondition: pull a target in and chain silence+suppress for a guaranteed kill
enemyKits.playWith: burst that deletes his pulled/suppressed target
enemyKits.playAgainst: respect Riplash range — stay spaced; cleanse/QSS the suppress

enemyKits.combo: Pounce → Rumble slow → Boulder Throw → Behemoth ult to brawl
enemyKits.winCondition: engage with Pounce, grow with Behemoth and out-sustain the fight
enemyKits.passive: ramping health regen for jungle sustain
enemyKits.playWith: follow-up damage while he front-lines and CCs
enemyKits.playAgainst: anti-heal and kiting beat his sustain brawl; burst him before Behemoth
